title: Text encoders: CLIP, T5 and LLM encoders

questions.q: In a causal encoder like GPT or Llama, why is the representation of the last token often used as the primary conditioning signal?
options: Because the last token is the only one that has seen all previous tokens, giving it the full context of the sentence.
Because the last token has the highest numerical value in the embedding space.
Because the first token is always masked out in causal models.
Because the last token is processed faster than the other tokens.
questions.answer: Because the last token is the only one that has seen all previous tokens, giving it the full context of the sentence.
questions.why: The lesson states: 'In a causal model, the last token has seen everything that came before it. It is the only token that has the full context of the sentence.'

questions.why: The lesson explicitly states: 'comfy/text_encoders/llama.py contains Llama2_, the core implementation for Llama models.'

questions.q: In the context of the attention mechanism described, what is the purpose of dividing the dot product $Q K^T$ by $\sqrt{d}$?
options: To increase the magnitude of the attention scores for better contrast.
To convert the scores into a probability distribution.
To remove the need for the Softmax function.
questions.why: The lesson explains the formula: 'We divide by $\sqrt{d}$ to keep the values stable.'
